items.title: Frugal living: budgeting and saving
steps: Write down all income and spending for one month (a notebook or an app). Know where your money goes.
Try the 50/30/20 guide: about 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings or debt. It is a rule of thumb. Adjust it to your situation.
Build an emergency fund first (a target of a few months of basic expenses) before you invest.
Electricity: unplug what you are not using, use LED bulbs and an inverter appliance, and read Meralco's energy tips (company.meralco.com.ph).
Water: fix leaks right away, and save rainwater for plants and cleaning.
Savings that earn: Pag-IBIG MP2 is a government-backed voluntary savings program. Check the current rules on the Pag-IBIG MP2 page.
Avoid 5-6 lending and online lenders that are not registered. Check the SEC list before you borrow.
Checklist: budget sheet · emergency fund started · 1 bill reduced · MP2 or savings account opened
steps_tl: Isulat lahat ng kita at gastos sa isang buwan (notebook o app). Know where your money goes.
Try the 50/30/20 guide: about 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% ipon/utang. It's a rule of thumb, adjust to your situation.
Unahin ang emergency fund (target: a few months of basic expenses) bago mag-invest.
Kuryente: tanggalin sa saksakan ang hindi gamit, gumamit ng LED at inverter, at basahin ang energy tips ng Meralco (company.meralco.com.ph).
Tubig: ayusin agad ang tagas, mag-ipon ng tubig-ulan para sa halaman at paglilinis.
Ipon na may tubo: Pag-IBIG MP2 is a government-backed voluntary savings program; check current rules on the Pag-IBIG MP2 page.
Iwasan ang 5-6 at online lending na hindi rehistrado; check the SEC list before borrowing.
Checklist: budget sheet · emergency fund started · 1 bill reduced · MP2 or savings account opened
items.tip: It does not have to be perfect. Consistency beats size. No investment has a guaranteed return.
items.tip_tl: Hindi kailangang perpekto; consistency beats size. Walang garantisadong tubo sa kahit anong investment.

items.title: Eco-friendly living
steps: Bring an eco-bag, a tumbler, and a food container to cut single-use plastic.
Buy refills or in bulk when you can. Avoid sachets.
Energy: turn off lights and air-conditioning when nobody is in the room, set the air-conditioner around 24–25°C, and unplug chargers.
Water: shorter showers, a bucket when washing a vehicle, and fix leaks.
Take public transport, bike, or walk when it is safe. Carpool.
Grow something, even a pot by the window (see the Permaculture and Urban farming guides).
Know the rules: EMB (DENR) handles air, water, and solid-waste laws.
Checklist: eco-bag · tumbler · 1 energy habit · 1 water habit · 1 plant
steps_tl: Magdala ng eco-bag, tumbler at baunan para bawas single-use plastic.
Bumili ng refill o bulk kung kaya; iwas sachet.
Energy: patayin ang ilaw/aircon kapag walang tao; set aircon around 24–25°C; i-unplug ang chargers.
Water: shorter showers, timba sa paghugas ng sasakyan, ayusin ang tagas.
Commute, bike or walk kung ligtas; mag-carpool.
Magtanim: kahit paso sa bintana (see the Permaculture and Urban farming courses).
Know the rules: EMB (DENR) handles air, water and solid waste laws.
Checklist: eco-bag · tumbler · 1 energy habit · 1 water habit · 1 plant
items.tip: Small habits you can repeat matter more than one big purchase.
items.tip_tl: Small, repeatable habits matter more than one-time big purchases.

items.title: Waste management at home (RA 9003)
steps: RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2001) requires segregation at source.
Biodegradable: food scraps, fruit peels, leaves. Compost them.
Recyclable: clean bottles, cans, paper, cardboard, and some plastics. Sell them to a junk shop or bring them to an MRF.
Residual (not biodegradable and not recyclable): sachets, diapers. These go to LGU collection.
Special waste: batteries, bulbs, medicine, paint, e-waste. Do not mix them in. Ask the barangay or LGU where to take them.
Compost: a container with holes, alternating green (food scraps) and brown (dry leaves, cardboard). Turn it weekly. Keep it moist, not soggy.
Learn your collection schedule and your barangay's MRF (Materials Recovery Facility).

Where to take it (verified 29 Oct 2026): SM Trash to Cash (recyclables for cash, first Friday and Saturday of the month), CORA Eco-Ikot (sachets and recyclables for points), Globe E-Waste Zero and SM Cyberzone bins (e-waste), and brand take-back such as Nespresso capsules. See Recycle and drop-off programs in the Directory.
Checklist: 4 containers · compost bin · collection day known · e-waste set aside
steps_tl: RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2001) requires segregation at source.
Biodegradable (nabubulok): tira-tirang pagkain, balat ng prutas, dahon → compost.
Recyclable (nare-recycle): malinis na bote, lata, papel, karton, ilang plastic → ibenta sa junk shop o dalhin sa MRF.
Residual (hindi nabubulok/hindi recyclable): sachets, diapers → para sa kolekta ng LGU.
Special waste: baterya, bumbilya, gamot, pintura, e-waste → huwag ihalo; itanong sa barangay/LGU kung saan dadalhin.
Compost: lalagyan na may butas, salit-salitan ng 'green' (food scraps) at 'brown' (tuyong dahon, karton); haluin linggo-linggo; panatilihing mamasa-masa, hindi basa.
Alamin ang schedule ng kolekta at ang MRF (Materials Recovery Facility) ng barangay mo.

Saan dadalhin (verified Oct 29, 2026): SM Trash to Cash (recyclables → cash, first Fri & Sat ng buwan), CORA Eco-Ikot (sachets at recyclables → points), Globe E-Waste Zero at SM Cyberzone bins (e-waste), brand take-back gaya ng Nespresso capsules. Tingnan ang 'Recycle & drop-off programs' sa Directory.
Checklist: 4 na lalagyan · compost bin · alam ang collection day · e-waste set aside
items.tip: Open burning of waste is prohibited under RA 9003.
items.tip_tl: Bawal ang open burning ng basura sa ilalim ng RA 9003.

items.title: Prepping and survival basics
steps: Go-bag (per person): water, ready-to-eat food, flashlight, extra batteries, radio, power bank, first-aid kit, medicines, copies of IDs in a zip bag, cash, clothes, a blanket, a whistle, a face mask, and hygiene items.
Family plan: a meeting place, a contact list written on paper, who will fetch the children or older relatives, and the barangay evacuation center.
Typhoon: watch PAGASA signals, charge devices, secure loose objects, and evacuate when told to.
Earthquake: Duck, Cover, and Hold. Stay away from glass. Afterward, go outside carefully and watch for aftershocks. Follow PHIVOLCS.
Flood: do not wade or drive through floodwater. Turn off the main switch if water is coming in. Watch for leptospirosis.
Fire: know two ways out, crawl under smoke, and call 911 or the BFP.
First aid: take first-aid training from the Philippine Red Cross.
Checklist: go-bag · family plan · evacuation center known · emergency numbers saved · first-aid kit
steps_tl: Go-bag (per person): tubig, ready-to-eat food, flashlight, extra batteries, radyo, powerbank, first-aid kit, gamot, kopya ng IDs sa ziplock, cash, damit, kumot, whistle, face mask, hygiene items.
Family plan: meeting place, contact list (sulat sa papel), sino ang susundo sa mga bata/lolo't lola, evacuation center ng barangay.
Bagyo: bantayan ang PAGASA signals; i-charge ang devices; itali ang maluluwag na gamit; lumikas kapag inutusan.
Lindol: Duck, Cover and Hold; lumayo sa salamin; pagkatapos, lumabas nang maingat at mag-ingat sa aftershocks. Follow PHIVOLCS.
Baha: huwag lumusong o magmaneho sa baha; patayin ang main switch kung papasok ang tubig; mag-ingat sa leptospirosis.
Sunog: alamin ang dalawang daan palabas; gumapang sa usok; tawag sa 911 o BFP.
First aid: kumuha ng first-aid training sa Philippine Red Cross.
Checklist: go-bag · family plan · alam ang evacuation center · emergency numbers saved · first-aid kit
items.tip: Emergency hotline: 911. Always follow the official advisory of your LGU and the NDRRMC.
items.tip_tl: Emergency hotline: 911. Sundin lagi ang opisyal na abiso ng LGU at NDRRMC.

items.title: What is permaculture?
steps: Permaculture means designing homes, gardens, and communities that work like nature. The term was coined by Bill Mollison and David Holmgren.
3 ethics: Earth care (care for the soil), People care (care for people), and Fair share (share the surplus and limit consumption).

Holmgren's 12 principles, in short: 1 Observe and interact. 2 Catch and store energy (rain, sun). 3 Obtain a yield. 4 Apply self-regulation and accept feedback. 5 Use and value renewable resources. 6 Produce no waste. 7 Design from patterns to details. 8 Integrate rather than segregate. 9 Use small and slow solutions. 10 Use and value diversity. 11 Use edges and value the marginal. 12 Creatively use and respond to change.
Zones (0–5): 0 the house, 1 closest (herbs and daily vegetables), 2 fruit and chickens, 3 main crops, 4 semi-wild, 5 wild.
Sectors: where sun, wind, flood, rainwater, and noise come from. Place plants and tools to match them.
A balcony start in the Philippine climate: pots of kangkong, pechay, chili, lemongrass, and oregano; recycled containers; mulch so the heat does not dry them out.
A backyard start: compost (see the Waste guide), a rain barrel, native or adapted plants (malunggay, kamote, saluyot, alugbati), and a layered food forest (tree, shrub, herbs, groundcover).
Checklist: 1 week of observation · sun and water map · compost · 3 easy crops · rain catchment
steps_tl: Permaculture = designing homes, gardens and communities that work like nature. Term coined by Bill Mollison and David Holmgren.
3 ethics: Earth care (alagaan ang lupa), People care (alagaan ang tao), Fair share (hatian ang sobra, limit sa konsumo).

Holmgren's 12 principles (simple): 1 Observe and interact (obserbahan muna). 2 Catch and store energy (ipunin ang ulan, araw). 3 Obtain a yield (dapat may ani). 4 Self-regulate and accept feedback. 5 Use renewables. 6 Produce no waste. 7 Design from patterns to details. 8 Integrate rather than segregate (pagsamahin). 9 Small and slow solutions. 10 Use and value diversity. 11 Use edges and value the marginal. 12 Creatively use and respond to change.
Zones (0–5): 0 bahay, 1 pinakamalapit (herbs, gulay araw-araw), 2 prutas/manok, 3 pananim, 4 semi-wild, 5 wild/kalikasan.
Sectors: saan galing ang araw, hangin, baha, tubig-ulan at ingay; ilagay ang tanim at gamit ayon dito.
Balcony start (PH climate): paso ng kangkong, pechay, sili, tanglad, oregano; recycled containers; mulch para hindi matuyo sa init.
Backyard start: compost (see Waste guide), rain barrel, native/adapted plants (malunggay, kamote, saluyot, alugbati), layered 'food forest' (puno → shrub → herbs → groundcover).
Checklist: 1 week observation · sun/water map · compost · 3 easy crops · rain catchment
items.tip: Start small. Related: Eco-friendly living, Waste management, Urban farming.
items.tip_tl: Start small. Related: Eco-friendly living, Waste management, Urban farming.

items.title: Hydroponics for beginners
steps: Hydroponics is growing plants in water with nutrients, without soil.
Kratky (the simplest, no electricity): a container with a lid, a net cup, a growing medium (for example coco coir), and nutrient solution. Leave an air gap as the water level drops.
DWC (Deep Water Culture): like Kratky, but with an air pump and air stone so the roots get oxygen.
NFT (Nutrient Film Technique): a thin flow of nutrient solution through PVC or gutter channels with a pump. This is more advanced.
Nutrients: use a hydroponic nutrient mix and follow the label. Watch pH (often about 5.5–6.5 for leafy greens) and EC/TDS with a meter.
Crops for the Philippine climate: lettuce (in shade or cooler spots), pechay, kangkong, mustard, and basil. Protect them from extreme heat and rain.
Materials: a styrofoam box or a bucket, net cups, coco coir, nutrient A and B, a pH kit, and optionally an air pump and a TDS meter.
Checklist: Kratky setup · seedlings · weekly pH check · harvest log
steps_tl: Hydroponics = pagtatanim sa tubig na may nutrients, walang lupa.
Kratky (pinakamadali, walang kuryente): container na may lid, net cup, growing medium (e.g. coco coir), nutrient solution; hayaang may air gap habang bumababa ang tubig.
DWC (Deep Water Culture): parang Kratky pero may air pump at air stone para may oxygen ang ugat.
NFT (Nutrient Film Technique): manipis na daloy ng nutrient sa PVC/gutter channels gamit ang pump; mas advanced.
Nutrients: gumamit ng hydroponic nutrient mix at sundin ang label. Bantayan ang pH (karaniwan ~5.5–6.5 para sa leafy greens) at EC/TDS gamit ang meter.
PH-climate crops: lettuce (sa malilim/mas malamig), pechay, kangkong, mustasa, basil; protektahan sa matinding init at ulan.
Materials: styro box o timba, net cups, coco coir, nutrient A+B, pH kit, (optional) air pump at TDS meter.
Checklist: Kratky setup · seedlings · pH check weekly · harvest log
items.tip: Free hydroponics and urban-agriculture courses: DA-ATI e-Extension. Related: the Urban farming guide.
items.tip_tl: Libreng hydroponics at urban-ag courses: DA-ATI e-Extension. Related: Urban farming course.

items.title: Planning an urban farm
steps: Space and sun: how many hours of sun does the spot get (most vegetables want about 6 hours)? Measure the space, and check whether a balcony can hold the weight.
Containers and vertical growing: recycled bottles, buckets, sacks; vertical racks or hanging pots to save space.
Budget: start with cheap materials and seeds. Record costs and harvests.
Water: a rain barrel, drip from recycled bottles, and water in the morning.
Soil: garden soil plus compost (see the Waste guide), and mulch.
Pest IPM: look every day, remove pests by hand, use companion plants (marigold, lemongrass), and avoid excess pesticide.
Harvest plan: staggered planting (sow every 2 weeks) so the harvest keeps coming.
Learn more: DA-ATI urban agriculture trainings and ATI e-Extension (free).
Checklist: sun map · 5 containers · compost · water plan · planting calendar
steps_tl: Space & sun: ilang oras ng araw ang natatanggap (karamihan ng gulay: ~6 oras)? Sukatin ang espasyo; check kung kaya ng balcony ang bigat.
Containers & vertical: recycled bottles, timba, sako; vertical racks o hanging pots para makatipid sa espasyo.
Budget: simulan sa murang materyales at seeds; i-record ang gastos at ani.
Water: rain barrel, drip mula sa recycled bottles, magdilig sa umaga.
Lupa: garden soil + compost (see Waste guide); mulch.
Pest IPM: obserbahan araw-araw, tanggalin nang mano-mano, companion plants (marigold, tanglad), at iwasan ang sobrang pesticide.
Harvest plan: staggered planting (magtanim kada 2 linggo) para tuloy-tuloy ang ani.
Learn more: DA-ATI urban agriculture trainings, ATI e-Extension (libre).
Checklist: sun map · 5 containers · compost · water plan · planting calendar
